Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

This is the top-rated game of the day, and it's not particularly close. A tightly-wound rubber match closes out the season series between the Cubs and Brewers, with Milwaukee riding a big NL Central cushion and eyeing a home sweep. Logan Henderson has quietly become one of the best young arms in baseball — sitting at 9-3 with a 2.48 ERA and a microscopic 0.79 WHIP across 83.1 innings — and his 8.73 pNERD backs that up, built on excellent strike-throwing and a stingy xFIP-. Gausman's been shakier of late but still owns a strong résumé; the two actually dueled six days ago, when these two starters combined for 14 innings and three earned runs in a 2-1 Cubs win. Both team offenses are lively — Chicago's power (led by a Pete Crow-Armstrong breakout) and Milwaukee's youthful, athletic lineup both grade out well in tNERD, with the Brewers boosted by strong fielding and bullpen work. At 18.03, this gNERD sits well above the historic 95th percentile and is the day's high mark, making it the easy pick if you only have time for one game.

Washington Nationals @ San Diego Padres, 1:10p

Summary

San Diego's playoff push meets Washington's fade in a series finale that's more watchable than the standings would suggest. The Padres are clinging to the final NL Wild Card spot, a game behind Arizona, while the Nationals limp into Petco Park trying to end a six-game losing streak in this finale, having let San Diego score four runs in the eighth to steal Tuesday's game. Walker Buehler continues his reclamation tour after bouncing between Boston and Philadelphia last year — his time in San Diego has "rehabilitated his career a bit", and he's been sharp lately, having allowed just one earned run on three hits over five innings against the Yankees in his last outing. His pNERD of 4.72 is middling but solidly above replacement-level theater. Opposite him, rookie lefty Jackson Kent is walking a tightrope: he's 1-3 with a 5.55 ERA across five starts since his August 12 debut, with 21 strikeouts and 19 walks — that command issue tanks his pNERD to 2.87. Team-wise, this is the real draw: San Diego's 9.64 tNERD is buoyed by a strong bullpen and above-average broadcast ratings, while Washington's 8.48 mark leans on youth and baserunning. Combined gNERD of 12.86 sits comfortably above the day's average — worth a look if you like playoff races with shaky rookie pitching thrown in.

Cincinnati Reds @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

The Dodgers roll out their best against a fading Reds club still clinging to faint wild-card hopes, and the pitching mismatch alone makes this worth a look. Los Angeles enters on a hot streak — the Dodgers have been playing their best baseball of the second half, winners of six straight and holding firm atop the NL West with an 88-57 record — while Cincinnati sits at 69-76, needing wins to keep any postseason hopes alive in September. Yamamoto is the headliner here, sporting a stellar 79 xFIP- and 8.29 pNERD (today's field averages just 4.76), backed by plus velocity and strikeout stuff; rookie Lowder, by contrast, is scuffling with a below-average xFIP- and a modest 3.74 pNERD, and carries a 5.43 ERA and 1.49 WHIP into this one. On the offensive side, the Dodgers' 7.85 tNERD (elite batting runs, strong bullpen) dwarfs Cincinnati's 5.11, though Elly De La Cruz's speed (88 runs, 25 steals) gives the Reds some chaos potential on the bases. At 12.50, this gNERD sits comfortably above the historical median and near today's average — solid, if unspectacular, watchability driven almost entirely by Yamamoto's arm and the Dodgers' late-season surge.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

Good sample of storylines. Let me write the summary now.

A pennant-race sleeper: the surging White Sox host a scrappy Pirates club, with just enough pitching intrigue to make it worth a glance. Chicago's stunning turnaround from three straight 100-loss seasons into an AL Central lead is the real headline here, and this game offers a decent, if unspectacular, viewing case, with today's 11.95 gNERD sitting a bit above the historic average of 10.81 but shy of today's own slate-topping games.

The White Sox carry the better team profile (8.41 tNERD), fueled by a young, cheap roster and solid barrel rates, though they've been quietly unlucky by -21 runs, suggesting better days could be ahead. Pittsburgh counters with excellent baserunning and a bullpen that's outperformed expectations, even if shaky fielding drags them down. On the mound, Davis Martin (4.90 pNERD) is returning from an IL stint for a right middle finger blister, activated on September 2, and is searching for his first win since mid-June. Lake Bachar (3.63 pNERD) brings solid strikeout stuff but shaky command. Both offenses have thump — Oneil Cruz's .506 xwOBA and Esmerlyn Valdez's .477 xwOBA give the Pirates real run-creation upside — so don't be shocked if this one gets loud.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Two division leaders, one big lineup showdown, and a Jax outing worth catching even if you skip the rest. Tampa Bay and Atlanta are both fighting for playoff seeding as September winds down, and while the pitching matchup is lopsided on paper, there's enough thump in both lineups to keep things lively.

Griffin Jax is the headliner here, sporting an 8.16 pNERD built on a sharp xFIP- and well above-average swinging-strike rate. He's performed at a high level recently, allowing one earned run or less in three of his last four starts. The opposing arm was unlisted at file time, though reports point to Reynaldo López working back into Atlanta's rotation - Atlanta is getting a key piece back at exactly the right moment - but without stats to go on, that half of the mound is a mystery box.

Offensively, Junior Caminero's been Tampa's engine while Matt Olson anchors Atlanta's power, and Truist Park's slight hitter-friendly tilt won't hurt either side. At 11.76, the gNERD sits a touch above the historical middle and roughly in line with today's average slate - solid, not spectacular, but Jax alone makes it worth a look.

Houston Astros @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Cristopher Sánchez is the headliner here, and his opponent's own numbers say so: expect a lopsided but oddly entertaining pitching mismatch in Philadelphia. Sánchez enters as the game's high point, an All-Star who started the 2026 Midsummer Classic for the NL and carries a 16-5 record with a 2.58 ERA into the start; more importantly for our purposes, his xFIP- of 61 and standout swinging-strike rate power a 10.19 pNERD, easily the best pitching mark on either roster today and well above the 95th-percentile threshold historically. Hunter Brown is a capable complement (4.65 pNERD, a mid-90s fastball helping offset a middling strike rate), but this is Sánchez's stage, even though Houston has actually enjoyed modest success against him, hitting .297 with 11 hits in 37 at-bats, and he strikes out Astros hitters at a rate well below his career norm. On the team side, neither club dazzles — Houston's tNERD is thin thanks to shaky baserunning and fielding, while Philadelphia's boost comes more from bullpen depth and broadcast appeal than its middling offense, whose batting runs are actually well below average. Add in that this is just the second meeting between these teams this season, with Houston having opened the series with a 6-5 win at Citizens Bank Park, and you get a game whose 11.41 gNERD sits a shade above the historical average — worth a look mainly for Sánchez, not much else.

Cleveland Guardians @ Baltimore Orioles, 3:35p

Summary

Baltimore's rotation is running on fumes and Cleveland is peaking, which makes this series finale more compelling than the box score would suggest. The Orioles have lost seven of their last eight, sit fifth in the AL East, and are trying to stay afloat in the wild-card race, while Cleveland has won seven of its last eight games on the road, pushing them to a 74-72 record. Foster Griffin, Cleveland's lefty, has been legitimately excellent: he's making his 29th start of the season, sporting a 15-4 record with a 3.26 ERA and 142 strikeouts in 160 1/3 innings. His 5.61 pNERD is well above average for today's slate, built on strong contact management. Shane Baz brings mid-90s velocity but a slower pace that dings his NERD a bit, and he enters at 5-15 with a 3.91 ERA, a 1.33 WHIP and 145 strikeouts across 163.1 innings in 28 starts. Cleveland's tNERD edges Baltimore's thanks to bullpen strength and a younger roster, though both offenses are middling. Camden Yards' quirks and a genuine form gap between the two clubs make this a decent, not spectacular, watch — roughly average on today's slate, comfortably above the historic median.

New York Mets @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

A rebuilding Marlins club with a young, cheap roster hosts a fading Mets team, and neither starter is going to make anyone forget prime Doc Gooden. Miami's tNERD of 9.21 stands out mostly because of good luck (they're outperforming their skill-based numbers, so some regression may be coming), a low payroll, and a young roster, while the Mets' tNERD of 5.65 is buoyed more by a strong bullpen and broadcast ratings than by actual hitting, which has been a genuine weakness. On the mound, it's a battle of the underwhelming: Stock's numbers are genuinely ugly — a 1.75 WHIP and 13 walks in just 26.1 innings, though his xFIP- suggests some bad luck is baked into that ugly line. Junk, meanwhile, has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his last five outings, but his NERD score is dragged down by a weak swinging-strike rate. New York enters having won the first two games of this series and won the first two games by scores of 9-4 and 7-5, so there's some series-finale drama, but at 10.47 this gNERD sits almost exactly at the historical median — competent, unremarkable, background-noise baseball.

Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

This one's a headliner: Jacob Misiorowski brings a 100-mph fastball and Cy Young-caliber numbers to a Brewers team chasing its fourth straight NL Central title, and the gNERD score of 20.24 backs that up as one of the best on the slate today (today's games top out at 20.24, well above the historic average of 10.81). Misiorowski's pNERD of 14.88 is elite even by exceptional standards—his xFIP- of 54 and a swinging-strike rate that dwarfs the league are legit, and his fastball has already rewritten the record books this year for pitch velocity. He's dominated Chicago this season, going 2-0 with a stingy ERA in three prior starts against the Cubs, though he did get roughed up for five runs in one of those outings—so he's not unhittable. On the other side, David Peterson (pNERD 5.31) has been homework since his midsummer arrival from the Mets, alternating flashes of grounder-heavy competence with second-half hard-contact trouble; he lasted only 3 2/3 innings last time he faced Milwaukee. Both lineups carry real thump—Chicago's fielding and batting runs are strong, and Milwaukee leads the NL in runs scored—giving this game high-scoring upside if Misiorowski falters, and a must-watch floor if he doesn't.

Chicago Cubs @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

A tight NL Central race gives this one stakes, even if the arms on the mound are more workmanlike than dominant. Milwaukee holds a seven-game lead over Chicago, and with the Brewers looking to lock up the season series for tiebreaker purposes, this rematch of last week's series at Wrigley carries some late-season weight. Chicago won the most recent meeting 2-1, splitting a four-game series after Milwaukee had taken the middle two games by lopsided scores. Neither bullpen is fresh — Milwaukee's pen got overworked in a 12-8 loss in Cincinnati while Chicago's did the same in a 10-3 blowout in Miami, so neither unit arrives rested. Milwaukee is also without Brandon Woodruff and lost Quinn Priester for the season, forcing more bullpen reliance — but the Brewers' actual bullpen NERD component is strong, offsetting that. On the mound, Boyd and Gasser are both middling by NERD (3.92 and 4.74, roughly average for today's slate), though Gasser gets a bump from being unlucky this year. The real juice here is the offense and depth on both sides — this gNERD of 14.47 sits well above the historical average and near today's high end, making it one of the better watches on the board.

Cincinnati Reds @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

A rookie-adjacent ace with a wipeout slider takes the mound against baseball's best lineup, and the Reds' bullpen plan alone is worth the price of admission. This game rates 14.25 on the gNERD scale, comfortably above both the historic average (10.81) and today's slate average (11.60), and it's easy to see why once you look past the standings.

The headline is Chase Burns, whose 10.38 pNERD is well above the 95th percentile historically — he's been outstanding in 2026 with a 1.16 WHIP and a 28.9% strikeout rate that ranks among the best in the National League, fueled by upper-90s velocity and elite whiff rates. There's a wrinkle worth watching: a right elbow flexor strain briefly sidelined him this summer, and the Reds have been managing his workload carefully ever since, which explains why Terry Francona plans to piggyback Brandon Williamson behind Burns to keep his innings down. The Dodgers' response is a mystery-box TBD, reportedly journeyman/rookie fill-in Emmet Sheehan, whose stuff has been hittable in the minors.

Team-wise, the Dodgers (8.11 tNERD) bring a top-tier offense and bullpen, riding a four-game win streak, while the Reds (5.01 tNERD) are scuffling but oddly barrel the ball well. Not a must-watch pitching duel on paper, but Burns alone makes it worth tuning in early.

Nick Pivetta's return from a five-month elbow absence is the whole story here, and it's a genuinely fun one to tune into. The Padres are activating Pivetta off the 60-day IL for his first big-league start since he walked off the mound mid-rehab back in April, and last year he finished sixth in NL Cy Young voting behind a 2.87 ERA. His final tune-up was encouraging — "4⅓ scoreless innings and seven strikeouts on 64 pitches" — though the team has him on a restricted pitch count, so don't expect length. No sample exists yet for our pNERD model, hence his 0.00, but the small-sample peripherals (13.5 K/9, sub-1.15 WHIP) suggest real swing-and-miss stuff if the elbow holds. Jake Irvin, by contrast, is a well-quantified mess this year — his xFIP- and shaky command drag him to a middling 3.61 pNERD, salvaged only by tough luck. The Padres own the far better bullpen and broadcast ratings, pushing tNERD to a strong 9.48, and Washington's baserunning and pop give it a respectable 8.65 too. Miami's stealthy playoff push meets a Mets team basically running out the string with an intriguing arm, and the pitching matchup alone makes this worth a look. Eury Pérez brings a 7.27 pNERD built on a 98 mph fastball, elite swinging-strike rate, and a still-youthful frame at 23 — a career-low hard-hit rate and career-best ground-ball rate show he's evolving from thrower to pitcher even as his strikeout rate dips. Opposite him is Jonah Tong, whose pNERD reads zero simply because there's no real big-league track record yet — the Mets promoted him for this game and likely the rest of the season after going 10-5 with a 1.43 ERA in the minors last year. Atlanta Braves @ Philadelphia Phillies, 10:05a

Summary

Jesús Luzardo is pitching like the best version of himself right now, and that alone makes this one worth clearing your schedule for. The Phillies lefty enters having been named NL Pitcher of the Month for August, and he's 5-0 with a 1.64 ERA across his last five outings, missing bats at an elite clip with 209 strikeouts on the season. His 10.51 pNERD is well above today's average of 5.91 and sits near the historic 95th percentile, backed by a filthy xFIP- of 70 and a fastball touching 96.5 mph — the run-prevention and swing-and-miss profile of a true ace. Grant Holmes is a serviceable if unspectacular counter, with a middling xFIP- and modest 3.57 pNERD, and reports note Holmes generates outs but invites baserunners at a higher rate than his counterpart.

The teams themselves are roughly average watchability-wise — both Atlanta and Philadelphia sit near league-median tNERD, though the Phillies get a bump from broadcast quality and Atlanta's bullpen has quietly been strong. Storyline-wise, Atlanta has already clinched the season series against Philadelphia, up 7-3 with four games left to play, and they've won three of the four meetings so far in this very series, giving this getaway-day finale some divisional pride on the line even with the standings largely settled. Not a must-watch offense, but Luzardo's stuff makes it worthwhile.

Noah Cameron is the actual draw here, and his 5.65 pNERD (comfortably above today's 5.91 average) reflects a quietly effective lefty who's allowed just six runs across 25 innings in his last four starts, including a one-hit, eight-strikeout complete-game shutout of the Angels on Aug. 16. Team-wise, Arizona's 76-68 wild-card push gives their tNERD a lift via strong baserunning and fielding marks, while Kansas City's 4.38 mark is dragged down hard by a shaky bullpen — though positive luck suggests their run prevention should actually improve. Overall gNERD of 10.32 sits almost exactly at the historical median, a solidly average watch elevated mainly by Cameron's arm.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Cincinnati Reds, 9:10a

Summary

A Brewers rotation arm chasing forearm-tightness redemption against a Reds bullpen that's been running on fumes — this one has enough moving parts to be worth a look, even if the pitching matchup is lopsided. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.84 reflects a genuinely fun team: strong baserunning, a shutdown bullpen, and a young, cheap roster that overachieves its payroll. Cincinnati checks in lower at 5.10, dragged down by weak batting runs and bullpen performance, though positive luck suggests some regression upward is coming. On the mound, Kyle Harrison (pNERD 10.64) brings excellent strikeout stuff and a tidy xFIP-, but he's trying to bounce back from a disastrous start, having allowed nine runs on 10 hits -- including five homers -- in 3 2/3 innings against the Cubs, with pitch-tipping suspected as a culprit. Brady Singer (pNERD 4.72) is the weaker link statistically, though Cincinnati emptied its bullpen across Friday and Saturday, with every one of the team's eight active relievers pitching in one of those two games — meaning length from Singer matters more than usual. Today's gNERD of 15.15 sits well above both the historical and today's-slate averages, making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board despite Cincinnati's rough season.

Detail

Washington Nationals @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

Cade Cavalli's return alone gives this game a story worth watching: a former top prospect back from Tommy John and finally healthy is squaring off against Tyler Glasnow, whose own career has been a rolling injury saga. Both teams post strong tNERD marks — Washington's 8.45 fueled by excellent baserunning and a young, cheap roster, LA's 8.19 driven by big-time batting production — and the pitching side is even better, with Glasnow's 9.18 pNERD the headline thanks to a sparkling xFIP- of 66. Cavalli isn't far behind at 7.82, riding a mid-90s heater and a stretch where he's allowed only five earned runs in his last six starts. This is Glasnow's first home start since returning from the injured list, adding some intrigue to how his surgically-rebuilt arm holds up. The Dodgers, despite losing six of their last nine games, still hold a comfortable lead atop the NL West, while the Nationals have lost five straight on the road and are fading from wild-card contention — so don't expect playoff desperation, just quality arms. At 16.82, the gNERD score sits well above both the historical average (10.81) and today's slate (10.87), making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Texas Rangers, 4:05p

Summary

Rasmussen and deGrom bring the ace stuff, and this one has October implications baked in — that's a rare combo worth clearing your evening for.

Tampa Bay rolls in at 84-57, holding a four-game AL East cushion, while Texas sits below .500 but still fighting for playoff position, so this series carries real weight beyond the pitching matchup. The Rangers hope the "vintage" Jacob deGrom returns for his next start, five days after the 38-year-old pitched one of the best games of his career. That gem saw him face the minimum through seven innings against Oakland, the first Rangers pitcher to do that since 2023. The stats back up the eye test — deGrom's pNERD of 10.82 is elite, built on nasty swinging-strike rates and mid-90s-plus heat, and it's boosted by some bad luck (a 4.00 ERA that his xFIP suggests he doesn't deserve). Rasmussen isn't far behind at 8.29, and Tampa's righty enters 14-5 with a 2.95 ERA, having gone 5-0 in six August starts. Team-wise, both sides are just okay, but with two frontline arms dueling, this gNERD of 14.66 ranks near the top of today's slate — prioritize the first few innings.

Jordan Walker delivered a two-run home run in the Cardinals' 13-8 win over Los Angeles earlier this week, so there's some offensive thump to watch for, even if the pitching matchup itself won't be the draw.

Toronto Blue Jays @ Kansas City Royals, 4:10p

Summary

I have enough here.

A wild-card scrap between a scuffling Toronto club and a Kansas City team playing out the string, with two veteran pitchers who've both seen better days. The Blue Jays are clawing for their playoat life while the Royals are just trying to spoil the party, and the pitching matchup does little to inspire confidence in either direction.

Toronto sits 13.5 games back in the division but is very much alive in the wild card conversation, having gone 21-13 since July 27, and they enter having gone 7-3 over their last ten games riding a three-game winning streak — including a Friday blowout where nine different Blue Jays recorded a hit. On the mound, Max Scherzer is the headline name but not the reason to tune in: Scherzer is 2-7 with a 6.16 ERA — a difficult stretch for a veteran who has been one of the game's most decorated starters, and his xFIP-backed pNERD of 1.37 reflects real skill decline, not just bad luck (well, actually some good luck, since his 23.0 luck score suggests he's earned an even worse line than his ERA shows). Seth Lugo is modestly more interesting statistically, his quick pace and respectable peripherals pushing him to a 4.14 pNERD, though he has struck out 118 batters but carries a 5.03 ERA of his own. Both teams' offenses and shaky bullpens (Kansas City's especially, a full two standard deviations below average) suggest a laugher is as likely as a pitcher's duel. At a 6.36 gNERD — well below both the historical and today's average — this one's a bottom-of-the-list watch unless you're a Jays fan sweating the standings.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Two aces, a division race, and a genuine ace-vs-ace duel make this the best watch on the board today. Chris Sale and Cristopher Sánchez sit at Nos. 3 and 2, respectively, in MLB.com's most recent NL Cy Young poll, and this is round two of their season series—their first meeting ended with Sánchez allowing three runs, all unearned, over six innings, while Sale countered with seven innings of one-run ball. The stakes are real too: the Braves and Phillies are entering a critical stretch with seven meetings in 10 games, and Atlanta currently holds a four-game lead in the NL East. Sale has been quietly dominant, having allowed more than three earned runs just once all season, with the Angels tagging him for six in four innings back in April, while Sánchez has been nails at home, going 11-1 with a 1.68 ERA in home starts this season. The gNERD of 15.75 sits in the upper tier both historically (95th percentile is 15.6) and among today's slate (season-high 15.75), driven almost entirely by two elite arms with xFIP- in the 60s and swinging-strike rates well above average. Neither team's offense is thrilling on paper, but with this pitching and this postseason context, that hardly matters.

Washington Nationals @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

Blake Snell, fresh off elbow surgery and looking every bit like his Cy Young self, makes this Dodgers-Nationals mismatch worth tuning in for despite the lopsided record. The gNERD of 15.72 sits well above both the historic average (10.81) and today's average (10.72), driven almost entirely by Snell's dominant return.

Since coming back from injury on August 11, Snell has made four starts, allowing a total of three runs over 23 innings for a 1.17 ERA, and he is yet to allow a home run this season. His 9.62 pNERD reflects elite swing-and-miss stuff backed by a sparkling xFIP-, comfortably in this dataset's upper percentiles. Across the mound, Jackson Kent has no track record to speak of statistically (pNERD of 0.00), but there's novelty here: Kent, who's coming off his 1st MLB win against Miami, will pitch on 6 days' rest, still just five career starts into his big-league career. The lopsided pitching matchup lines up with a lopsided season — Washington's playoff hopes are fading quickly, as the Nationals now sit 7.5 games back of the final NL Wild Card spot. Both offenses grade out well by tNERD (8.52 and 8.29), with Washington's baserunning and the Dodgers' slugging doing the heavy lifting, but a hobbled bullpen for Washington (among the league's worst by Bullpen Runs) suggests if this one gets late and close, Nationals fans might want to look away.

Chicago Cubs @ Miami Marlins, 4:10p

Summary

A wild-card race game featuring a lefty who can't stop giving up home runs against a bottom-of-the-rotation righty — but the surrounding rosters make this one worth a look. The Cubs enter clinging to the top wild-card spot, trailing Philadelphia by half a game, and they trail the Philadelphia Phillies by a half game for the top wild card spot in the National League — every game counts down the stretch. Imanaga carries the better pNERD (6.16 vs. 2.37) thanks to strong strikeout stuff and a favorable xFIP-, but he's stuck in an ugly home-run rut, having allowed 11 dingers in just 29.1 IP since July 31 — the most in baseball — with 33 total homers on the season. Junk is a fine story as a well-traveled journeyman finally holding a rotation spot, but his stuff (weak swinging-strike rate, so-so command) doesn't inspire much confidence, and he's compiled a 6-4 record and 4.17 ERA with 77 strikeouts over 110 innings this season for Miami. Where this game earns its solid 14.04 gNERD — comfortably above today's 10.72 average — is the team quality: Chicago's elite fielding and offense pair with Miami's youthful, underperforming (and thus due for better luck) roster to make both sides genuinely watchable, even if the pitching matchup itself is lopsided.

entry.content:

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:15p

Summary

Milwaukee's charging into Wrigley with the majors' best rookie storyline on the mound, and this one lands near the top of today's slate for good reason. Logan Henderson has been a revelation, carrying a 9-2 record, 2.48 ERA, and 3.29 FIP across 14 starts, and he's been remarkably stingy with free passes — a 2.48 ERA and 0.83 WHIP across 76.1 innings while walking just 14 batters all season against 86 strikeouts. His pNERD of 8.77 reflects that combination of elite command and swing-and-miss stuff, well above today's average. Gausman, by contrast, has been the definition of inconsistent since arriving from Toronto — a 3-1 record with a 5.14 ERA and 4.08 FIP over five Cubs starts, alternating rough outings with a couple of gems — though his pNERD still checks in at a respectable 6.77, boosted by some bad luck that suggests better days ahead. On the team side, Chicago's tNERD (10.44) is carried by standout batting and fielding runs, while Milwaukee's (9.82) leans on baserunning and a strong bullpen, though the Cubs' pen is a real liability. Combined, this gNERD of 17.90 sits comfortably above both the historic 95th percentile and today's field — genuinely one of the day's best watches.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

Tarik Skubal at Dodger Stadium against a Cardinals lineup missing key pieces is about as good a watchability bet as you'll find on the slate today. The Dodgers ace, now in his second month in LA after the trade-deadline blockbuster, has been every bit the marquee arm: Skubal has a 3.00 ERA and 37 strikeouts over 30 innings as a Dodger, and owns a 2.84 ERA with 153 strikeouts across 126.2 innings pitched overall this season. His last time out, he threw six innings against the Detroit Tigers, giving up one earned run while allowing four hits. His pNERD of 12.23 is driven by elite whiff and strike rates plus a stingy xFIP-, and it ranks near the top of today's pitcher scores. Opposite him is Quinn Mathews, making his fifth start for the Cardinals, sitting at 1-2 with a 5.03 ERA and 20 strikeouts in 19 2/3 innings — a rookie with no track record yet, hence the flat 0.00 pNERD. The Dodgers' offense (tNERD 8.16) and bullpen give them the clear team-level edge over St. Louis's older, lighter-payroll but well-fielding Cardinals (6.35). With a gNERD of 15.87, well above both the historic and today's averages, this is a legitimate top-of-the-slate watch, carried almost entirely by Skubal.

The Marlins try to complete a sweep in Kansas City, and Wacha's recent form makes that a tougher ask than the standings suggest. Kansas City hasn't lost a start from Wacha in more than three weeks, and he's riding real heat: his most recent start was his best of the season, working eight innings against Cleveland with four hits, no walks and a season-high 10 strikeouts. Alcantara, meanwhile, has been the opposite story—the Marlins have struggled to win with their ace on the mound, losing four straight starts he's made—even though his stuff remains loud, with a 97-plus mph fastball driving his pNERD edge. Both starters pound the zone and rarely walk anyone, which oddsmakers think points to a lower-scoring affair, though the first two games of this series produced nine and 15 runs, and Kansas City is without its established closer, so that low-scoring read is far from guaranteed. On the NERD side, Miami's tNERD (9.14) towers over Kansas City's (4.08), largely because the Royals' bullpen has been a sinkhole while Miami's roster skews young, cheap, and unlucky enough to expect better days ahead. Soriano, acquired by the Jays at the deadline, brings the day's best pNERD (7.14) on the strength of mid-90s velocity and a strong strikeout arm, though his ERA and FIP since joining Toronto sit around 4.13 and 3.73 — solid, not spectacular. Bibee, meanwhile, owns an ugly 5-14 record, and while that's partly bad luck, his SIERA is a career-high and strikeout rate a career-low, and his pNERD of 3.17 reflects the genuine decline. He's allowed three or more runs in four of his last five starts, posting a 4.20 ERA in August — worth watching if Toronto's lefty-heavy lineup, who've combined to average 1.94 home runs per nine off Bibee thanks to a 10% barrel rate against lefties, can tee off early.

On the team side, Cleveland's tNERD (7.03) benefits from a young, cheap roster while Toronto's (3.16) gets dragged down by lackluster barrel rates on both sides. The 10.25 gNERD lands almost exactly at the historical median and comfortably below today's slate average of 11.63, so treat this as a decent-not-urgent watch — good for Soriano's stuff, but no reason to clear your schedule.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

This is about as good as it gets on paper, and the numbers back it up: a 20.60 gNERD score, comfortably atop today's slate and near the historic ceiling. Jacob Misiorowski, sporting a pNERD of 15.28 built on triple-digit velocity and elite swing-and-miss rates, is making his first start of September, with an opportunity to beat the Cubs for the third time this year, entering with a Majors lead in ERA, strikeouts, WHIP and opponents' average. He's now just a few weeks from what appears to be an NL Cy Young-winning season, 14-5 with a 1.73 ERA and 2.14 FIP over 151 innings, and even Pedro Martinez is publicly hyping him up. David Peterson, by contrast, offers a modest 5.51 pNERD and is mostly along for the ride, though since being acquired by the Cubs in late June he's pitched to a better 3.90 ERA and 4.31 FIP than his ugly season-long numbers suggest. Both tNERD marks sit well above average — Chicago's fueled by strong batting and fielding runs, Milwaukee's by baserunning and bullpen depth — and with the Brewers holding an eight-game NL Central lead, this is a marquee pitcher plus two solid lineups. Watch it.

New York Yankees @ Los Angeles Angels, 6:38p

Summary

A legitimate Cy Young frontrunner takes the mound against a last-place club that's found itself a genuine problem in a lefty with a hot streak — this one's better than the standings suggest. Cam Schlittler enters as the American League frontrunner to win the Cy Young, posting a 2.09 ERA through 163.2 innings this season, and he's been especially nasty lately — 2-0 with a 1.13 ERA in his last four starts — with his 10.47 pNERD backed by elite velocity (98 mph) and strikeout stuff pushing his xFIP- to an excellent 71. On the other side, Reid Detmers isn't just a sacrificial lamb: he's 4-8 with a 1.55 ERA in his last eight starts for Los Angeles, and has historically owned this Yankees lineup, having given up one run in 15.1 innings in his career against the Yankees. That backstory bumps his pNERD to a respectable 7.30. The Yankees carry real team quality (8.29 tNERD, elite barrel rate) while the Angels' offense and defense are both well below average, dragging their tNERD to 1.26 — but with two quality arms dueling, don't expect much scoring. At a combined 13.66 gNERD, this sits above the historic average and is one of the more watchable matchups on today's slate.

This game is worth catching mainly for Yamamoto, since the Cardinals are countering with a bullpen game and no named starter at all. St. Louis just hung 13 runs and five homers on LA a night earlier—Thomas Saggese hit two, Jordan Walker added a two-run shot—so there's a decent chance Wednesday is as much about revenge as pitching. Yamamoto, though, is in the middle of a strong stretch: he's looking to pick up where he left off after a dominant August, when he posted a 1.95 ERA with 35 strikeouts over 32.1 innings, and sits at 12-8 with a 2.56 ERA and 153 strikeouts across 158 innings on the season. His 8.14 pNERD is driven by strong strikeout-and-command indicators and above-average velocity, easily the best pitching mark in this matchup and well above the historic median. A gNERD of 13.62 sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, making this one of the better watches on the board, mostly because of Yamamoto rather than any single storyline.

entry.content:

Detail

Toronto Blue Jays @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:40p

Summary

Cleveland's Gavin Williams brings some of the best raw stuff in baseball to this one, and that alone should be enough to get this game bumped up your watchlist. The Guardians righty has racked up 204 strikeouts and a sparkling 3.98 ERA (and a much shinier 69 xFIP-) this year, pairing 97-mph heat with elite whiff and strike rates that produce the day's best pNERD score, 12.37 — well above today's average of 5.57 and squarely in the sport's upper tier. Opposite him is Spencer Miles, a 2026 rookie for Toronto still getting his feet wet in the majors, but his 78 xFIP- and mid-90s velocity make him a solid, sneaky-good foil rather than a laugher. Team-wise, neither Toronto nor Cleveland hits for much thump — both post barrel rates among the worst in the sample — but Cleveland's young, cheap, athletic roster (tNERD 7.14) offsets Toronto's star-power-but-underwhelming-output group (tNERD 3.60). Add it up and you get a gNERD of 15.63, comfortably above both the historical average (10.81) and today's slate (11.17), making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board, driven almost entirely by pitching.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Two division rivals, a Wrigley Field showdown between NL Central leaders, and both offenses swinging hot bats make this a legitimately watchable Tuesday matinee-turned-primetime affair. The Cubs and Brewers enter this four-game series as division heavyweights, with the Cubs ending August and beginning September with a key four-game set against the NL Central leaders, and Chicago coming off a statement win, having crushed Milwaukee 17-3 in the series opener on Monday. The Cubs' tNERD (10.81) is elite thanks to a lineup that's been mashing all year and a defense that's been vacuuming up outs, though their bullpen has been a genuine liability all season. Milwaukee counters with plus baserunning and a strong pen, plus a roster that's younger and cheaper than most.

On the mound, Robert Gasser is a fill-in success story — he stepped in to finish out Dustin May's start against the Mets last week, going 5 1/3 innings with one run allowed on six hits and two walks, striking out six to earn the win. His pNERD of 4.88 reflects modest peripherals but a bit of positive regression coming. Matthew Boyd, an All-Star last year, has cooled lately — he's taken the loss in two of his last three starts, allowing 13 runs over 17 1/3 innings against the Cardinals, Mariners, and D-backs — though he's historically dominant at Wrigley. Combined gNERD of 14.78 sits comfortably above today's 11.17 average, making this one of the sharper watches on the slate.

San Francisco Giants @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Two three-time All-Stars trading pitches at PNC Park is reason enough to tune in, and Paul Skenes' velocity and swing-and-miss stuff make him the best arm on the mound anywhere in baseball today. The Pirates (67-71) have won two straight and are clinging to fringe playoff hopes as they open a season-critical six-game homestand, while the Giants arrive limping defensively but riding some positive batted-ball luck that suggests better days ahead. Skenes, still chasing his first career win over San Francisco, brings a 10.34 pNERD built on elite xFIP-, a mid-90s heater, and youth on his side — comfortably the headliner here, especially with Skenes hasn't recorded a win since July 19 despite the strong underlying numbers. Webb counters as a solid if unspectacular complement, his 5.35 pNERD held down by modest velocity and whiff rates even as his xFIP- stays sharp. Team-wise, Pittsburgh's baserunning and bullpen give it a real edge over a Giants club dragged down by shaky fielding and baserunning. At 13.26, the gNERD lands comfortably above today's 11.17 average and well into the upper half of all games historically — a legitimately watchable one, anchored by Skenes.

Michael McGreevy (pNERD 3.57) is the more watchable arm, young and durable at 142.1 innings, but neither offers swing-and-miss thrills. With a gNERD of 8.96, below today's 11.17 average, this is a game to check in on rather than clear your schedule for.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's runaway NL Central lead versus Chicago's fading hope makes this a genuine race-relevant tilt, and it comes with the top gNERD score of the day — well above even the historically hot 95th percentile. The Brewers, division leaders at 85-52, roll into Wrigley for the first of four with the Cubs sitting eight games back after briefly closing to 3.0; Bleacher Nation frames the whole set as a series where the Cubs were roughly five to six games back before briefly cutting it to 3.0 games on August 14, only for that hope to fade fast. Both lineups grade out near the top of the league in tNERD, with Chicago's fielding and batting runs standing out and Milwaukee's baserunning and bullpen doing the heavy lifting, though the Cubs' shaky bullpen (tNERD component of -1.40) is the one real soft spot.

On the mound, Kyle Harrison brings a sparkling xFIP- and a well-below-average pace that makes him one of the more watchable arms around, and he's been nearly untouchable in stretches — striking out 10 Pirates over five innings on August 5, then holding Seattle to two hits across five scoreless frames on August 18 — though he hasn't finished a sixth inning in his last four starts as Milwaukee manages his workload. Clay Holmes, meanwhile, has been arguably better lately: he came over from the Mets at the trade deadline and has been outstanding since joining the rotation on August 8, posting a 1.96 ERA across 23 innings, including seven scoreless on two hits against Arizona last time out. His modest pNERD reflects a lower strikeout rate than you'd expect given those results, but the underlying skill marks (xFIP-, strike rate) are solid enough to make this a legitimately compelling pitching matchup atop a high-stakes divisional series.

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Miami’s Ryan Gusto has quietly been terrific lately, and Washington counters with a rookie making his first career start — that combination alone makes this worth a look, even if the standings say otherwise. Gusto has pitched 9 2/3 scoreless innings over his past two starts, including 5 2/3 shutout innings in a 4-0 win against the Boston Red Sox, and his pNERD of 4.65 (driven mostly by a strong strike rate) reflects genuine recent quality, not just a hot streak. Across the plate, Will Dion makes his first major-league start after 18 relief appearances, which changes the entire shape of Washington's pitching plan — a true unknown quantity with a pNERD of 0 simply because we have no starter track record to grade yet. The bigger story is the teams: both Miami (9.46 tNERD) and Washington (8.54 tNERD) land comfortably above the historical average, pushing this to a 13.83 gNERD — solidly ahead of the historic 10.81 mean and above today's own 11.07 average, thanks largely to strong baserunning and youth on both sides. Washington's bullpen has been dreadful with a collective 4.60 ERA over the last 10 games, and opposing hitters have hit 12 home runs against Washington's pitchers — expect fireworks if it's still a game by the seventh inning.

Seattle Mariners @ Boston Red Sox, 3:45p

Summary

Both Seattle and Boston are limping toward September, but the pitching matchup makes this one worth a look. Payton Tolle, Boston's 23-year-old rookie lefty, has been the story of the Red Sox summer: Boston counters with rookie left-hander Payton Tolle, who has ascended to nearly the top of the rotation as the season has evolved, and has been especially impressive during August, including eight shutout innings against Toronto and a career-high 14 strikeouts against Oakland. That form shows up in his 9.82 pNERD, built on elite strike-throwing and a nasty whiff rate, plus the youth bonus of doing it all at 23. George Kirby isn't far behind at 7.63 pNERD, thanks to plus velocity and strong command, and he's coming off a bounce-back outing where he allowed just one earned run over 7⅔ innings while striking out nine against Philadelphia. On the team side, Boston's tNERD (6.83) benefits from a strong bullpen and some positive batting luck, while Seattle's 1.76 mark reflects rough fielding and baserunning numbers, and the Mariners are on a four-game losing streak heading into Fenway. The 13.02 gNERD lands comfortably above average both historically and among today's slate, driven almost entirely by the pitching — this is a start-focused watch, not a slugfest.

deGrom's underlying stuff still says ace, even if his recent results say otherwise, making this one worth catching despite two last-place-ish clubs.
